name: How do I know if my pool shell needs repair before resurfacing?

mainEntity.name: What signs mean the pool shell must be repaired before new plaster or tile?
mainEntity.text: What signs mean the pool shell must be repaired before new plaster or tile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before resurfacing, the shell should be inspected for structural issues that could undermine the new finish. Warning signs include obvious cracks, sections that sound hollow when tapped, prior patch repairs, ongoing water loss, or areas where the surface has separated from the substrate. If the underlying shell is unstable, resurfacing alone will only hide the problem temporarily. That is why reputable contractors inspect carefully after draining and before applying any finish. In older Los Angeles pools, hidden damage often shows up during this stage, especially where plumbing penetrates the shell or where shifting soil has stressed the structure. If shell repair is needed, it should be completed first and allowed to cure properly before new plaster or tile goes in. Homeowners should treat shell repair as a structural investment, not an optional upgrade, because it directly affects how long the renovation lasts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Large cracks, hollow-sounding areas, persistent leaks, delamination, or uneven movement in the pool structure can mean the shell needs repair before resurfacing. Surface finishes should not be installed over active structural issues, because the new material may crack, fail, or separate early.
